english: A stack of books sits crooked on the floor, half-buried under layers of dust.
The blue light from windows appears to land upon the surface and stick.
As if it is not real.
You recognize the binding style.
These are late Arcane Era.
One tome is clearly arcane - the cover bears ward-marks that make your eyes itch.
Doesn't seem like there's any danger here, right now at least.
If you wanna check out some books, go for it. I'll chill for a while.
Meek says, old master books are free for checking!
But if read wrong passage, big hurt! Remember!
The books wait where you left them.
Decipher the warded tome.
E-These books are not worth the headache.
Old master has ward on all!
Spell cast delayed spell! Hurt big if not careful!
Then just leave them alone?
The knowledge will be worth it. Surely.
The spell brightens your ability to read these chaotic books.
Well done. This will surely make understanding the journal easier as well.
The wards recognize your competence. They part like curtains.
Inside, you find a treatise on sensory magic. Illusions.
This Hagginshags was studying the relationship between perception and reality.
Rigorously. Mathematically.
Hundreds of pages of experiments, of the mixing of illusion and divination.
(Look over his results.)
He posits the mind does not receive reality - it constructs it.
Each moment, your senses gather fragments. Color. Sound. Pressure. Heat.
Then something deeper - something he calls the 'interpretive layer' - assembles those fragments into a coherent world.
The question he asks, not quite so directly: what happens when you tamper with that layer?
Not showing someone a fake image. Not casting darkness over their eyes.
Rather, reaching into the mechanism itself through esoteric means, thus adjusting the assembly.
This does not appear too far-fetched.
It does not. This seems to align well with the scholarly basis of your education.
However, the next part does not.
The last half of this tome: Throughout many trials, mostly performed on himself, you gather...
This man who calls himself a Hagginshags - he shows results pointing towards a measurable conduit within every String. One visible only through this altered layer.
'THE BLOOM OF JOR LIES UPON EACH CASTER,' he writes. 'ALL CHANNELED THROUGH THE GATES. INVISIBLE. HIDDEN. EVEN THE OUTER GODS ARE BLIND.'
'HOW ELSE WOULD THE LICH SUSTAIN HIMSELF? HOW ELSE DO THE POCKETS BOTH INCREASE BELOW AND DECREASE ABOVE?'
'ONLY I CAN SEE THE TRUTH - ONLY I CAN MASTER THE RELIC LEFT BY UMBRAMEEXUS. ALL I NEED IS TO LOCATE IT. THAT ONE WORD. ONE KEY TO UNLOCK A WORLD OF TOTAL DOMINANCE IN THE NEW ERA.'
'ALL I NEED IS POWER WORD: EBB.'
(Stare at the last page.)
Madness.
The type of madness only born from revealed truth.
New master has read old master's book?
Meek is very impressed!
(Close the tome, carefully.)
The wards seal themselves behind you. Satisfied, perhaps, that you treated their contents with respect.
The wards do not recognize you.
You push anyway. A scholar's arrogance.
(Try to close it.)
The book bites.
Pain - of the immaterial kind - lances through your skull.
For a split second you perceive the color of your own name. The sound of the number seven. The weight of yesterday.
Then it passes, leaving you nauseous and hollow.
The tome's covers snap shut. The wards glow smugly.
New master must be careful!
Old master left many nasty tricks...!
(Stagger back from the desk.)
